meta.title: Well Profiler App for the Open .well Format
meta.description: Welldot (formerly Well Profiler) is a free app for water well data in the open, versioned .well format — construction and geological profiles, pumping tests, operation, permits and water quality, exported as PDF reports.
featureList: Create, visualize and export geological and construction well profiles
Pumping tests with semi-log, Theis recovery and step-test charts
Operation, production, permits, water quality and continuous level loggers (.well v2.4)
Accepts incomplete field and legacy records — a missing value means unknown, never zero
Extensible with x- fields, x- blocks and institutional profiles

editorMeta.title: Well Profile Editor
editorMeta.description: Free browser-based well profiler app to create, visualize, and export geological and construction well profiles as open, versioned .well files.

hero.body: Free editor for the whole record of a well: construction and geological profiles, pumping tests, operation, permits and water quality, exported as PDF. A simple, versioned JSON, readable by any language.

format.intro: Today, well data lives in PDFs that don't talk to each other. The {well} file is a simple, versioned format to change that — a single JSON that fully describes a well, from construction and geology to pump tests, installed pumps, meters and production, permits, water quality and maintenance history, designed as an {standard}.

props.title: Drawing
props.body: Construction and geology at real scale, drawn the same way by any tool that reads the file.

props.title: Record
props.body: Predictable structure to archive and version well data, ready for submission and auditing.

props.title: Research
props.body: Organized metric fields allow cross-referencing and comparing wells across aquifers, regions, and eras.

props.title: Open
props.body: Human-readable JSON, public specification, and permissive license — free to use, extend, and contribute.

props.title: Pump tests
props.body: Raw test readings plus versioned interpretations — transmissivity, storativity, specific capacity — each tied to the tests it came from. See § III.

props.title: Operation & history
props.body: Installed pumps, meters, produced volumes and operating regime, water-use permits with their conditions, water-quality samples, continuous water-level series from installed loggers, and a log of maintenance and incidents across the well's working life.

intention.body: Today, a water well's data exists in many places: in the driller's notebook, in the consultant's spreadsheet, in the PDF report submitted to the licensing authority. Each in its own format, each {unreadable}. {welldot} and the {well} format were created to solve this.
intention.originNote: This project began as {wellProfiler}, a tool to draw well diagrams. It's growing into something broader: an open platform for the entire lifecycle of well data — not just the drawing.

pillars.title: Live editor
pillars.body: Tables linked to the drawing. Edit a layer, see the profile redrawn at real scale.

pillars.title: Open format
pillars.body: Human-readable JSON, public specification, and Apache 2.0 license. Implement in any language.

pillars.title: Submission-ready
pillars.body: PDF reports with your branding, the sections you choose and the profile at real scale across pages, in English or Portuguese.

tests.intro: Every level measurement and pumping test is an entry in an append-only {ledger}: spot measurements, constant-rate and step-drawdown tests, air-lift, recovery and more. Readings are stored as taken, and drawdown, s/Q, Q/s and other parameters are calculated automatically.
tests.chartCaption: Sample step-drawdown test, drawn by the editor's charts.

cards.title: Tests as recorded
cards.body: Steps with rate and duration, level readings over time and recovery after the pump stops.

cards.title: Versioned interpretation
cards.body: Each analysis records its method, analyst, source tests and results — T, S, K, specific capacity, recommended maximum flow. Several can coexist.

cards.title: Analysis editor
cards.body: The editor already reads analyses and shows the current aquifer state. Creating and editing them in the app is on the way.

contexts.text1: A single human-readable text file: archivable in folders, versionable in git, indexable in databases, {aiEm}. The core is strict where it matters — {si}, {wgs}, English keys — and {flexible} everywhere else.
contexts.text2: The repository includes a ready-made {skill}: point any agent to {repo} and it operates the format natively.

incomplete.intro: Well data is rarely complete. A 1987 report with only the depth and an air-lift yield, a registry without coordinates, a log with no lithology, a permit still without a number: each is already a valid {well} file. Almost every field is optional, open fields take any text, and a missing field means {unknown} — never {zero}. In the field and in old archives, knowing what is missing is information too.

rules.title: Almost everything is optional
rules.body: Name, coordinates, construction date, driller, lithology, tests, permits: each block and each field goes in when it exists. Construction blocks can be empty lists. An event needs only an id, a type and a date; a permit, a type and an authority.

rules.title: Suggested values, free text
rules.body: Casing material, drilling method, permit type, maintenance type, well use: the format recommends a vocabulary for interoperability, but open fields accept any value. Values outside it take the x- prefix and are kept and shown as written.

rules.title: Absent is unknown
rules.body: No regime means unknown flow, not zero. No status change means unknown status, not active. Production before the first meter reading is unknown.

rules.title: Gaps are data too
rules.body: Missing details and inconsistencies become warnings for review, never a rejection. The record stays in the file with its history, and what is not known stays visible instead of being filled with made-up values.

extensible.intro: A driller, a consultancy, a water utility, a university or a regulator: {anyone} can add what their work needs, without asking permission and without breaking anyone else's files. The spec requires every reader to keep these extensions on load and save. And what proves useful to many can become part of the format itself.

levels.title: Your own fields and blocks
levels.body: Any object takes fields with the x- prefix, and the file takes whole new top-level blocks: a state registry number, a company's internal code, gas monitoring at a mine.

levels.title: Profiles for institutions
levels.body: An agency, a company or a research network publishes a JSON Schema that requires extra fields, narrows vocabularies or sets its own x- extensions. Files declare it under profiles. Failures are warnings, and an unreachable profile never blocks a file.

levels.title: From x- to the standard
levels.body: An x- value that proves useful across many sources can be promoted to canonical: x-slug_test becomes slug_test, and both forms stay valid until the next major version. Changes to the core start as an open issue with the data, its real-world source and why no field can carry it.

horizon.intro: v2.4 covers geological, construction and hydrodynamic profiles — pump tests, aquifer analysis, continuous level logger series, pump installations, meters, production and operating regime, water-use permits and their conditions, water quality, general attachments and operational history. The specification evolves openly, and these are the gaps already mapped for the next versions.

props.title: Native .las
props.body: Import and storage of LAS geophysical logs (resistivity, gamma ray, caliper), side by side with the lithological profile.

props.title: Linked wells
props.body: References between files: observation wells for storativity, and one permit shared by several wells instead of repeated in each.

props.title: Multilingual text
props.body: Descriptions and notes tagged with their language, so the same file can carry Portuguese, English or Spanish text — plain strings stay valid.

props.title: Water quality assessment
props.body: Interpreted judgments such as water class, hydrochemical facies and fitness for use, stored next to the samples they come from.

props.title: Offline packages (.wellz)
props.body: One ZIP with the .well file and its attachments — reports, photos, permit scans — at relative paths, each checked by its sha256, to carry a whole well to the field or archive it without links. Already defined in v2.4; coming to the editor.

tools.intro: welldot is a set of small, independent packages. Use the editor, or pull just the piece you need into your own stack.

cards.title: \@welldot/core
cards.body: Types, Zod validators, JSON Schema and serialization for the .well format, plus its vocabularies — materials, permit types, water-quality parameters and limit sets. The foundation everything else builds on.

cards.title: \@welldot/utils
cards.body: Analysis of a .well file: geometry and volumes, aquifer hydraulics and pumping-test series, production by period and permit deadlines, water-quality derivations such as ion balance, Piper and Stiff.

cards.title: \@welldot/render
cards.body: The D3-based SVG renderer that draws every profile on this site at real scale, with a configurable theme — embeddable in any web app.

cards.title: \@welldot/pdf
cards.body: Customizable PDF reports on pdfmake: branding, watermark, page layout, theme, section toggles and order, en/pt labels. Works without any UI framework.

cards.title: \@welldot/vue
cards.body: Vue 3 base components for .well editors, with the Welldot theme and a Nuxt module.

cards.title: Profiler app
cards.body: This editor, source and all. Nuxt 4 + Vue 3, deployed at welldot.org — fork it or read how it's built.

boreHole.title: Bore Hole
boreHole.drillingMethodInfo: Drilling method used to open this bore hole interval. Pick one of the suggestions — rotary, percussion, cable tool, auger or air hammer.
boreHole.drillingMethodFreeText: This field is free text: if the method is not in the list, just type it (e.g. reverse circulation, sonic, jetting) and it will be saved as-is.

wellCase.title: Casing
wellCase.typeInfo: Material of the casing that lines the well and holds the bore hole walls, e.g. PVC, geomechanical PVC, carbon steel or stainless steel.
wellCase.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the material is not in the list, just type it (e.g. HDPE, blank steel pipe) and it will be saved as-is.

reduction.title: Reduction
reduction.typeInfo: Material or shape of the reducer that connects the two diameters, e.g. PVC, geomechanical PVC, carbon steel, conical or stepped.
reduction.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the material is not in the list, just type it (e.g. conical, stepped) and it will be saved as-is.

centralizer.title: Centralizers
centralizer.typeInfo: Kind or material of the centralizers clamped to the casing to keep it centered in the bore hole, e.g. spring bow, rigid, polymer, carbon steel or stainless steel.
centralizer.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the type or material is not in the list, just type it and it will be saved as-is.
centralizer.descriptionInfo: Optional notes about these centralizers, such as manufacturer, model, material or how they were installed.
centralizer.hint: One row per interval. Use the same depth in From and To for a single centralizer; leave spacing empty if unknown.

wellScreen.title: Screen
wellScreen.typeInfo: Material of the screen that lets water into the well, e.g. PVC, geomechanical PVC, carbon steel or stainless steel.
wellScreen.typeFreeText: This field is free text: if the material is not in the list, just type it and it will be saved as-is.
wellScreen.slotTypeInfo: Screen design, e.g. continuous slot (Johnson, wire-wrapped), slotted, bridge slot, louver, perforated or Nold type.
wellScreen.slotTypeFreeText: This field is free text: if the type is not in the list, just type it and it will be saved as-is.

holeFill.title: Hole Fill
holeFill.typeInfo: Role of the material in the annular space between casing and bore hole wall: gravel pack is the filter gravel around the screens; seal is the cement or bentonite that isolates the annulus against contamination.
holeFill.descriptionInfo: Material actually used in this interval, e.g. grain size of the gravel (1–2 mm quartz gravel) or seal material (cement grout, bentonite pellets).

general.name: Well Name
general.wellTypeInfo: Indicates the type of structure the well is, according to its construction (e.g. tubular, hand dug, horizontal, infiltration gallery). It is not the drilling method, nor what the well is used for: use Well Purpose for that. Artesian is a hydraulic condition, detected from the water levels.

artesianDeprecated.message: "Artesian" is deprecated as a well type since .well v2.1 — it is a hydraulic condition, not a construction method. Pick the construction method instead; a flowing artesian condition is recorded as a negative static level in the hydrodynamic events.

general.flowingArtesian: Flowing artesian — latest static level is above ground
general.clickOrDragPin: Click the map or drag the pin

wellIds.title: Well Identifiers
wellIds.primaryTooltip: Primary identifier — the canonical ID for this well

info.label: About well identifiers
info.title: What are well identifiers?
info.what: Other codes this same well has in external databases and registries. They make the .well file compatible with those systems, so the well can be cross-referenced and matched across different sources.
info.exampleGrant: Water-use permit (outorga) number issued by the water resources agency
info.exampleCompany: An internal code used by a company, utility or driller
info.fields: Authority is the name of the registry or institution that issued the code (pick a suggestion or type your own). ID is the code exactly as issued; keep leading zeros and separators (e.g. SP-0042819).
info.primary: Use the radio button to mark the main identifier. If none is marked, the first one is treated as the main one. Each authority + ID pair must be unique.

general.attachmentsInfo: Files about the well as a whole, such as the drilling report or an as-built drawing. Attachments of pumps, tests and history entries stay on their own records.

waterQuality.title: Water quality
waterQuality.noLimitSet: Pick a limit set in the Water quality tab to check compliance.

alerts.permitPendingRenewal: Permit {number} expired on {date}; renewal under review.
alerts.waterExceedances: {n} parameter(s) outside {set} limits in the {date} sample.

fields.author: Author
fields.eventsInfo: Events holding the data produced or observed in this entry, e.g. the level measured or the pumping test performed.
fields.statusInfo: The latest status change sets the current status of the well.
fields.samplesInfo: Water samples collected or concerned by this entry.

events.title: Hydrodynamic Events
events.comingSoon: Full editing available in the Hydrodynamic tab

hydrodynamicEvents.title: Hydrodynamic Events
hydrodynamicEvents.ledgerNote: Chronological ledger — new records are appended, not overwritten.

analyses.inDevBody: The Analyses tab will allow entering aquifer test results (transmissivity, specific capacity, storage coefficient).

hydrodynamicEvents.retractedInfo: A later event corrects this one. It stays in the file but no longer counts.
hydrodynamicEvents.correctionInfo: This event corrects an earlier one.

logger.noTimezone: The well has no time zone set, so times are read in your browser's zone ({zone}).

columns.datetimeInfo: Local time as YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss in {zone}, or an RFC 3339 instant with offset.

validation.datetime: use YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss or an RFC 3339 instant

import.title: Import readings from CSV

help.title: What the file should look like
help.rows: One reading per row, as exported by the logger software (CSV or plain text).
help.columns: Needed columns: the date and time (one column, or a date column and a time column) and the level. A pressure column is optional. Other columns, such as temperature or conductivity, are ignored.
help.dates: Pick the date format the file uses. A date that carries a UTC offset (2026-07-01T00:15:00-03:00) keeps it; otherwise the well time zone applies.
help.values: Columns can be separated by comma, semicolon or tab, detected automatically. Values can use a decimal comma (23,58) or point (23.58). The level can be depth to water or the water column above the sensor, which pressure transducers usually report.
help.header: Title or header lines at the top are fine: set how many to skip in "Header rows".
help.example: Example (semicolon, decimal comma, two header lines):
help.exampleMapping: Map it as: header rows 2, date column 1 (DD/MM/YYYY), time column 2, value column 3 as water column above the sensor, pressure column 4.

import.noTimezone: The well has no time zone set, so times are read with this UTC offset.
import.needSensorDepth: Enter the sensor depth to convert water column to depth.
import.summaryEmpty: No readings found with this mapping
import.replaceMessage: This drops the {count} readings already in the series.

charts.title: Charts
charts.empty: Not enough readings to draw charts.

logger.mixedLevels: This well pumps, so the series can mix static and pumping levels. Read it together with production and pump installations.

view.title: Hydrodynamic event
view.clockInfo: Δt restarts at each step; t runs from the start of the first step.

attachments.documentTypeInfo: What the document is (.well v2.3). Optional — leave empty when unsure.

pump.title: Pump installations
pump.intro: One entry per installation. A pump pulled and reinstalled gets a new entry with the same serial number. The current pump is the one without a removal date.
pump.submergenceInfo: Intake depth minus the latest dynamic level.
pump.submergenceNegative: The intake is above the latest dynamic level.

fields.typeInfo: Solar is a power source, not a pump type. Free text is allowed.
fields.removedAtInfo: Leave empty while the pump is installed.
fields.serialInfo: Links reinstallations of the same unit.
fields.intakeDepthInfo: Depth of the pump intake from ground level. The profile draws the pump ending here.
fields.ratedPowerInfo: Stored in kW; shown in the unit chosen in Settings. 1 cv = 0.7355 kW · 1 hp = 0.7457 kW.
fields.riserDiameterInfo: As-built outer diameter of the riser pipe.

warnings.intake_below_well_bottom: The intake is deeper than the well.
warnings.intake_in_screen: The intake sits inside a screen interval.
warnings.multiple_open_installations: More than one installation has no removal date.
warnings.removed_before_installed: The removal date must be after the installation date.

meter.title: Meters
meter.intro: One entry per installation of a totalizer (water meter). Device facts only: every register value, including the installation and removal readings, is a reading in Production.
meter.deleteConfirmWithReadings: This meter has readings in the production ledger. They stay in the file but will no longer resolve to a meter. Delete it anyway?
meter.readingsInfo: Record the register values at installation and removal as meter readings in Production, dated at these instants.

fields.serialInfo: A meter removed and reinstalled gets a new entry with the same serial number.
fields.removedAtInfo: Leave empty while the meter is installed.
fields.maxReadingInfo: Largest value the register shows before rolling over to zero. Used to derive the volume across a rollover.

regime.title: Operating regime
regime.intro: How the well is intended to run from a given moment. A change of regime is a new entry; the latest one already in effect is the regime in force. A stopped well is a status change in the history log, not a zero flow.
regime.unknownInfo: Leave a field empty when it is unknown — an empty field never means zero.

fields.effectiveFromInfo: Unique within the block. There is no end date: the next regime replaces this one.

production.title: Production
production.intro: Append-only ledger of water produced: meter readings and declared volumes. Entries are never edited — a correction is a new entry that retracts the original.
production.correctInfo: The correction is saved as a new entry that retracts this one. The original stays in the file but no longer counts.
production.deleteInfo: Deleting removes the entry from the file. To fix a wrong value, prefer a correction, which keeps the history. Delete anyway?
production.noMeters: Add a meter first to record its readings.

fields.readingInfo: Register value. Choose the volume unit in Settings to enter readings of meters that count in liters or gallons — they are stored in m³.
fields.methodInfo: How the volume was estimated (flow × time, energy use…). Descriptive only: estimated volumes count only where no meter reading covers the period.

totals.totalInfo: Metered plus estimated volumes. Meters take precedence over estimates.

production.unknownIntervals: {n} interval between readings has an unknown volume (the register went down and the meter has no register capacity). | {n} intervals between readings have an unknown volume (the register went down and the meter has no register capacity).
production.noPeriods: No volume can be derived yet.
production.retractedInfo: A later entry corrects this one. It stays in the file but no longer counts.
production.correctionInfo: This entry corrects an earlier one.

wellStatus.title: Well status
wellStatus.unknownInfo: The status is derived from “Status change” entries in the history log. None has been recorded yet.
wellStatus.derivedInfo: Derived from the latest “Status change” entry in the history log.

permit.title: Permits
permit.intro: One entry per legal instrument. The attached document is authoritative. A renewal is a new permit that supersedes the previous one; status and condition deadlines are derived.

fields.typeInfo: A renewal is not a type: create a new permit of the same type that supersedes the previous one.
fields.statusInfo: Administrative situation set by the authority. Leave "Granted" for an issued permit: its validity status is then derived from the dates.
fields.identifierInfo: Identifier of the granted instrument (portaria, license code…), as written in the document. Empty while the permit is only requested.
fields.requestIdentifierInfo: Protocol or process identifier of the request, as assigned by the authority.
fields.validFromInfo: Leave empty when valid from the issue date.
fields.validUntilInfo: Leave empty when there is no fixed expiry.
fields.renewalRequestedAtInfo: A renewal filed on or before the expiry keeps the permit active while it is pending.
fields.volumeLimitsInfo: Only volumes stated in the document. Volumes implied by flow × time are derived, never stored.
fields.monthlyScheduleInfo: When a schedule exists, months left empty have no abstraction granted.
fields.supersedesInfo: The permit this one legally replaces (renewal).

permit.grantDetailsInfo: filled once the permit is granted

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.descriptionInfo: Text of the condition as written in the document.
conditions.responsibleInfo: Person or team accountable for meeting this condition.
conditions.noStartDate: Needs an issue or start date to resolve.
conditions.scheduleInfo: Fulfillments marked here are saved with the permit.

fulfill.title: Condition fulfilled
fulfill.author: Fulfilled by
fulfill.info: Recorded in the condition's fulfillments. Attach the proof of submission as condition evidence.
fulfill.sampleInfo: Water sample whose analysis fulfills this condition.

history.title: History
history.info: Administrative steps of the permit: filing, process movements, notifications, fees, inspections, decisions.
history.dueDateInfo: For actionable steps (a fee to pay, a notification to answer). Past due and not done raises an alert.
history.deleteConfirm: Remove this step from the permit history?

view.timelineEmpty: No history steps or fulfillments recorded.

warnings.valid_until_before_valid_from: The expiry date is before the start date.
warnings.supersedes_unresolved: The superseded permit does not exist in this file.
warnings.supersedes_cycle: The supersedes chain loops back on itself.
warnings.overlapping_validity: Another permit of the same type overlaps this one.
warnings.daily_operating_time_normalized: A daily operating time above 24 h was read as 24 h.
warnings.monthly_above_max: A monthly value is above the permit maximum.
warnings.duplicate_month: A month appears more than once in the schedule.
warnings.duplicate_volume_period: A volume period appears more than once.
warnings.duplicate_condition_id: Two conditions share the same id.
warnings.condition_due_conflict: A condition has both a fixed date and a relative deadline; the fixed date wins.
warnings.invalid_duration: A condition has an invalid duration.
warnings.missing_identifier: Fill in the permit identifier or the request identifier.
warnings.granted_without_identifier: A granted permit has no permit identifier.
warnings.duplicate_history_id: Two history steps share the same id.
warnings.duplicate_fulfillment_id: Two fulfillments of a condition share the same id.
warnings.unmatched_fulfillment: A condition fulfillment matches no deadline of this permit.
warnings.missing_timezone: The well has no time zone; deadlines use the offset written on each date.

warnings.meter_removed_before_installed: The removal date must be after the installation date.
warnings.overlapping_meters: This meter is installed at the same time as another one.
warnings.duplicate_meter_id: Two meters share the same id.
warnings.reading_meter_unresolved: The meter of this reading does not exist in this file.
warnings.reading_outside_installation: This reading is outside the meter installation period.
warnings.reading_rollover_unknown: The register went down and the meter has no register capacity: the volume of this interval is unknown.
warnings.duplicate_production_id: Two production entries share the same id.
warnings.corrects_unresolved: The corrected entry does not exist in this file.
warnings.corrects_cycle: The correction chain loops back on itself.
warnings.estimate_period_invalid: The period end must be after its start.
warnings.estimated_overlaps_meter: This estimated volume overlaps meter readings; the meter takes precedence.
warnings.duplicate_regime_id: Two regimes share the same id.
warnings.regime_duplicate_effective_from: Another regime starts at the same instant.
warnings.regime_exceeds_permit: The regime in force is above the flow or daily operation granted by the active permit.
warnings.log_category_field_mismatch: This entry has fields that belong to another category.
warnings.log_reference_unresolved: A referenced pump, meter or event does not exist in this file.
warnings.log_after_decommission: This entry is dated after the well was decommissioned or abandoned.
warnings.missing_maintenance_type: This maintenance entry references data but has no maintenance type.
warnings.missing_status: This status change has no status.
warnings.analysis_uses_retracted_event: This analysis uses an event that has been retracted.
warnings.daily_operating_time_normalized: A daily operating time above 24 h was read as 24 h.
warnings.analysis_uses_logger_series: This analysis uses a logger series as a test.
warnings.logger_reading_below_sensor: A logger reading is deeper than the sensor.

waterQuality.title: Water quality
waterQuality.intro: Append-only ledger of water samples and their field and laboratory results. Samples are never edited — an amended report or a data revalidation is a new sample that retracts the original.
waterQuality.correctInfo: The correction is saved as a new sample that retracts this one. The original stays in the file but no longer counts.
waterQuality.retractedInfo: A later sample corrects this one. It stays in the file but is excluded from derivations.
waterQuality.correctionInfo: This sample corrects an earlier one.
waterQuality.deleteInfo: Deleting removes the sample from the file. To fix a wrong value, prefer a correction, which keeps the history. Delete anyway?
waterQuality.deleteBlocked: Referenced by a correction, a duplicate/split or a history log — it cannot be deleted. Record a correction instead.
waterQuality.compareAgainstInfo: Limits are never written to the .well file. Pick a bundled limit set to highlight exceeding results. Values are transcribed from the cited source and must be checked against the official document before regulatory use.

card.formationWaterInfo: The sample depth lies within a screen interval and below the static level.
card.notFormationWaterInfo: The sample depth lies outside the screens or above the static level — it may represent stagnant casing water.

errors.title: The sample cannot be saved:
errors.idTaken: Another sample already uses this id.
errors.labNameRequired: The laboratory name is required when any laboratory field is filled.
errors.pointTypeRequired: Choose the sampling point type to record a device, depth or pump.

fields.idInfo: Unique within the file. Duplicates, splits, corrections and history logs point to the sample by this id.
fields.sampleTypeInfo: Routine sample or QA/QC sample. Use an x- prefix for other types.
fields.parentSampleInfo: Required for field duplicates and split samples: the sample they replicate.
fields.campaignInfo: Free identifier grouping the samples of one sampling round.
fields.sequenceInfo: Orders samples taken at the same instant (e.g. a vertical profile).
fields.samplingMethodInfo: How the well was purged before collection.
fields.staticLevelEventInfo: Hydrodynamic event holding the water level measured at collection.
fields.preservationInfo: Preservation and packaging, free text (e.g. HNO₃ to pH < 2, cooled to 4 °C).

samplingPoint.title: Sampling point
samplingPoint.deviceInfo: What collected the sample. The purge itself is described by the sampling method.
samplingPoint.pumpInstallationInfo: Pump installation sampled at its discharge. The sample depth then comes from the pump intake depth.
samplingPoint.linkPumpAtCollection: Link the pump installed at collection: {pump}
samplingPoint.pumpNotInPlace: This pump was not installed when the sample was collected.
samplingPoint.pumpDepthInfo: Depth derived from the pump installation intake depth.
samplingPoint.depthInfo: Point depth of the sampler intake, from ground level.

purge.title: Purge
purge.stabilizedInfo: Field parameters were stable before collection.
purge.readingsInfo: Field parameters read while purging. The final values at collection go in the results, measured in the field.

result.unitInfo: Required for custom (x-) codes, in UCUM (e.g. mg/L, ug/L, uS/cm).

warnings.value_form_mismatch: The value form does not match the parameter (presence on a numeric code, or a value on a presence code).

warnings.analyzed_before_collection: Analyzed before the sample was collected.
warnings.received_before_collection: Received by the laboratory before the sample was collected.

warnings.duplicate_sample_id: Another sample uses the same id.

waterQuality.editTooltip: Edit in place — only to fix typing errors
waterQuality.editWarning: Editing changes the original record in place, with no trace of what it said before. Use it only to fix typing errors made when entering the data. For an amended lab report or a data revalidation, use Correct instead: it saves a new sample that retracts this one and keeps the history.
waterQuality.editConfirmInfo: The changes replace what was recorded for this sample, and the previous values are not kept. Continue only if you are fixing typing errors; for an amended report, cancel and use Correct.
